### [Stateless MCP has recaptured my interest (and inspired mcp-explorer and datasette-mcp)](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/31/stateless-mcp/#atom-everything)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-07-31

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) 2.0, or 2026-07-28 specification, introduces a stateless design, simplifying client/server implementations and enhancing scalability for LLM agent frameworks.

- Stateless MCP (2026-07-28 specification) replaces the two-request stateful model (initialize session, then call tool) with a single HTTP request for tool calls.
- Legacy stateful MCP required a POST to /mcp with "method": "initialize" to get a Mcp-Session-Id, followed by another POST with the session ID to "method": "tools/call".
- Stateless MCP uses HTTP headers like MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28, Mcp-Method: tools/call, and Mcp-Name: search, along with a single JSON body for the tool call.
- The stateless design eliminates the need for server-side state management of session IDs, improving scalability and simplifying routing.
- mcp-explorer is a new stateless Python CLI tool for interactively probing MCP servers, demonstrated with `uvx mcp-explorer list https://agentic-mermaid.dev/mcp`.

**Why it matters:** The simplified stateless design makes MCP tools easier to audit and control, enabling smaller models to drive them effectively and reducing implementation complexity for developers.

`mcp` `stateless` `llm` `protocol` `api`
